takeaway: Insulin promotes protein synthesis and drives potassium into cells, which is why it treats hyperkalaemia.

question.text: Which is a feature of the action of insulin?
question.say: Which is a feature of the action of insulin?

answer.say: The answer is: it promotes protein synthesis.

lines.text: Insulin the builder stacks the bricks of protein.
lines.say: Insulin is the builder, stacking bricks of protein, one on top of the other.
That is protein synthesis, and insulin promotes it.

lines.text: It also drives potassium into cells.
lines.say: (laugh) Look at the potassium ions running through the door. Insulin drives potassium into cells.

lines.text: That is why insulin treats hyperkalaemia.
lines.say: That is why insulin is used to treat hyperkalaemia.

lines.text: Calcium and phosphate are handled by parathyroid hormone and vitamin D, not insulin.
lines.say: Calcium and phosphate metabolism belongs to parathyroid hormone and activated vitamin D, not insulin.
